title: Bi-Continuous W-Rich Refractory High Entropy Alloy-Cu Composite: Toward Material Innovation of Nuclear Reactor Coolant System.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: A mixture of W-rich refractory high-entropy-alloy powders (e.g., W–Mo–Ta–Nb–V system) blended with elemental Cu powder
recollection.intervention: Guess: Powder-metallurgical processing (ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering or hot isostatic pressing) to densify and induce phase separation
recollection.structure: Guess: A bi-continuous (interpenetrating) microstructure in which both the W-rich HEA phase and the Cu phase form continuous, three-dimensional networks
recollection.mechanism: Guess: During densification, the low-melting Cu wets grain boundaries of the refractory HEA and capillary forces drive infiltration, yielding spinodal-like decomposition into two continuous phases that share interfaces for load transfer and thermal conduction
recollection.results: Guess: At room temperature, thermal conductivity ≈250 W/m·K, yield strength ≈800–900 MPa, fracture toughness ≈25–35 MPa·m^0.5, and significantly improved neutron‐irradiation tolerance compared to conventional stainless steels or pure Cu.

score.note: The proposed powder-metallurgy route is incorrect; the paper used molten-Cu liquid-metal dealloying of an as-cast WTaVTi precursor. The recollection identifies a bicontinuous RHEA–Cu network, but this is essentially stated by the title and omits the directionally aligned Cu channels, phase fractions, and ~300 nm W-rich interlayer. The wetting/capillary-infiltration mechanism is wrong, and the reported conductivity and mechanical/irradiation values do not match the paper.
